answer: Cross-epoch behavioural consistency rule: an identity's action distribution must stay within a similarity band across epochs. A fresh key that shifts behaviour abruptly from the prior epoch fails, unlike a pigment that stays stable under rotation. Each identity must clear a minimum activity summit over several epochs before gaining weight, so a raven swarm of fresh keys pays full epoch-warmup costs per identity and still gets filtered. Attacker cost is repeated full warmup plus the loss of all keys that fail the drift check.
